title: control-plane: add deployment component version + compatibility report endpoint (for private installer prechecks)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Private deployments: Control plane now exposes a signed/consistent component version + compatibility report endpoint used by the private installer precheck framework.
description: Summary: Adds a control plane endpoint for Private deployments to report (a) installed component versions and (b) compatibility signals required by the private installer upgrade prechecks. This unblocks deterministic upgrade planning in the installer and reduces reliance on ad-hoc kubectl scraping. Motivation: The Private upgrade workflow requires a single source of truth for "what is currently running" and whether an intended target is compatible (esp. schema migration downgrade constraints and version skew rules). The installer precheck runner (ENG-2316) will call this endpoint to produce a stable JSON report and provide actionable remediation messages. Endpoint: GET /api/private/v1/deployment/compatibility Report shape (high-level): { "deploymentId": "...", "generatedAt": "RFC3339", "components": [ { "name": "control-plane", "version": "1.28.3", "build": "...", "status": "ready" }, { "name": "runtime", "version": "..." }, { "name": "gateway", "version": "..." }, { "name": "observability-agent", "version": "..." } ], "migrations": { "schemaVersion": "2025.01.0", "downgradePolicy": "forward-only|reversible", "forwardOnlyMigrations": ["2025_01_14_add_migration_metadata"] }, "compatibility": { "minInstallerVersion": "0.19.0", "supportedTargetRanges": "[1.28.x -> 1.29.x]", "warnings": [ ... ], "errors": [ ... ] } } Notes: 1) This is a read-only endpoint and does not perform target selection. The installer computes the actual plan; the control plane provides the current-state and migration guardrails. 2) Compatibility outputs are intentionally conservative. We include "warnings" (non-blocking) vs "errors" (blocking). 3) Authorization: requires Private operator/admin scope (same gate as existing /api/private/* endpoints). 4) Stability: response includes explicit field names and avoids leaking internal k8s resource names where possible; we also added a small contract test to prevent accidental renames. Implementation details: - Introduced a DeploymentVersionReporter in the control plane service layer to aggregate versions from: (a) control plane build info; (b) helm release annotations (gateway/runtime); (c) observability agent chart version; (d) DB migration metadata table (added in follow-up PR) when present. When migration metadata is not available (older installs), we return downgradePolicy="unknown" and a warning instructing operator to upgrade to a minimum patch before attempting major upgrades. - Added a compatibility rule evaluation module that emits: version skew checks (control plane vs gateway/runtime), minimum installer version requirement (so older installers fail fast with a clear message), and downgrade constraints (if any forward-only migrations are detected). - Added structured audit log entry for endpoint access at INFO level with request id + actor id (no sensitive payload logged). - Added Prometheus metric: private_deployment_compatibility_requests_total{result="ok|error"} and histogram private_deployment_compatibility_duration_seconds. Testing: - Unit tests for rule evaluation (skew detection, downgrade policy handling). - Integration-ish test using a fake helm release store + fake migration metadata. - Added OpenAPI spec entry and golden snapshot of response fields. Rollout/compat: - Endpoint is additive. - Installer will be updated to prefer this endpoint when available; otherwise it will fall back to legacy discovery for one release (tracked in ENG-2315). - Known limitation: runtime version is derived from chart/appVersion; if customer manually patches images without updating chart metadata, we will flag "config drift" warning (not error) and point to docs. Screenshots/snippets: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer …" https://<control-plane>/api/private/v1/deployment/compatibility | jq .compatibility.errors -> []
commits: compatibility: implement version skew + installer min version rules
metrics/audit: add request metrics + access audit log entry
tests: add rule evaluation unit tests + response contract snapshot
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Like the direction. Two questions: (1) Can we guarantee field stability for installer consumption (no accidental rename)? (2) How do we handle older installs without migration metadata without creating false confidence about downgrade safety?

Benji Okafor (author): (1) Added a response contract test + OpenAPI snapshot; also documented that installer must treat unknown fields as ignore, but we won't rename existing fields. (2) For older installs, downgradePolicy returns "unknown" plus a warning; installer will treat "unknown" as blocking for rollback and surface remediation (upgrade to >= patch that includes migration metadata).

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure we don't log the entire compatibility payload in audit logs; a few of these fields could reveal internal topology. Also add a duration metric so we can catch slow DB calls during upgrades.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated audit logging to include only endpoint name, actor, request id, and result. Added private_deployment_compatibility_duration_seconds histogram + counter with result label.

Quentin Harris (review): For version skew rules: can we codify explicit boundaries? Right now it looks like any mismatch is a warning. We should error when control plane is newer than gateway by >1 minor, and warn for patch drift.

Benji Okafor (author): Implemented: error when major differs; error when minor differs by >1; warning for patch drift; warning when runtime chart appVersion differs from image label (best-effort). Added tests for the boundary cases.

Michael Nguyen (review): The migrations object currently includes forwardOnlyMigrations but the table doesn’t exist everywhere yet. Please guard reads and do not fail the endpoint if the table is missing; return warning instead. Also, please align naming with upcoming migration metadata PR so we don’t churn fields.

Benji Okafor (author): Guarded the query; if relation missing we return downgradePolicy="unknown" and warnings[]. Naming aligned to the metadata table proposal: schemaVersion, downgradePolicy, forwardOnlyMigrations.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved. Thanks for adding the contract test and making unknown downgrade policy a safe default.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved with metrics/audit changes.
Merge outcome: Squash merge into main by Benji Okafor after CI green.
